previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic systolic heart failure was admitted for periumbilical abdominal pain, weakness, dizziness, and hiccups. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was evaluated with serial troponins, a nuclear stress test showing transient ischemic dilatation and global hypokinesis with an ejection fraction of 41%, and subsequent cardiac catheterization revealing hypertensive heart disease without coronary artery blockages. Abdominal pain was attributed to diabetic gastroparesis. The patient underwent scheduled hemodialysis, remained hemodynamically stable, and had medication adjustments including reduced doses of furosemide, losartan, and sevelamer, along with a switch to Hexavitamin. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, monitor for recurring symptoms, and adhere to his updated medication regimen.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with longstanding history of DM type I and 
multiple complications, ESRD on dialysis, admitted w/ hiccups 
and mild hyponatremia. His hiccups had been continuous for a 
total of 7 days prior to admission and were interfering with his 
ability to sleep and eat. He has had episodes of hiccuping in 
the past, but never for this long.
.  
# Hiccups: Differential for hiccups include toxic-metabolic or 
drug-related disorders, central nervous system disorders, 
psychogenic factors, and vagus and phrenic nerve irritation. No 
pathology on CT to suggest macro-irritation of diaphram. While 
uremia can cause hiccups, 45 is not exceedingly high for patient 
to think this is the cause. 
-During his hospitalization, pt was given IV Thorazine at slowly 
increasing doses as a known treatment for hiccups.  He was also 
scheduled for his routine dialysis on ___ in the afternoon.  
Near the end of his HD treatment, his hiccups resolved. On the 
morning of discharge, he was still without hiccups and resting 
comfortably for the first time in many days.  He will be sent 
home with a prescription for Thorazine 25 mg PO Q6-8hrs prn 
hiccups.  Per his nephrologist he has had multiple episodes of 
hiccups for at least 6 months but not to this extent.  This 
should be readdressed at his upcoming PCP appointment as higher 
doses of thorazine were concerning for antipsychotic effects.
.  
# Hyponatremia: He did not appear grossly volume overloaded on 
exam, although given history of ESRD, most likely etiology is 
volume overload given renal disease and systolic/diastolic heart 
failure, and elevated BNP.  True volume depletion with poor PO 
intake in the setting of hiccups with concurrent lasix use may 
also be a possible etiology. His lasix was held during his 
inpatient stay, and he was dialyzed as per his outpatient 
regimen.
.

poorly controlled DM with retinopathy, neuropathy, nephropathy 
and gastroparesis. Followed at ___.  No active issues during

had glucose checks.  He was continued on his home regimen of

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Hiccups for one week.  High pressure diaphragmatic process.

Comparison is made to ___ examination.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis with oral contrast only.  Intravenous contrast was withheld due to
patient's renal function.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were evaluated.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH ORAL CONTRAST ONLY:  Limited evaluation of the lung
bases is normal, without any evidence of pneumonia, effusions or septal
thickening.  Small simple pericardial effusion is again noted and there is
stable appearance to probable underlying cardiomegaly.  Non-contrast
evaluation of the liver, spleen, pancreas, stomach, small bowel, adrenal
glands, and kidneys is unremarkable.  There is suggestions of gallstones.  No
free air, free fluid, or pathologically enlarged lymph nodes.  Atherosclerotic
disease is again noted within the intra-abdominal aorta and its branch
vessels. Previously identified ascites has resolved.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH ORAL CONTRAST ONLY:  Other than very mild rectal wall
thickening which may be related to underdistention and appears chronic, the
bowel is normal.  No evidence of obstruction. Urinary bladder and prostate are
within normal limits.

BONE WINDOWS:  Probable enchondroma within the left iliac is unchanged.  No
malignant-appearing osseous lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No etiology for persistent hiccups identified.  Visualized lung bases and
upper abdomen appear unremarkable with resolution of previously identified
septal thickening and intra-abdominal ascites.

2.  Trace pericardial effusion persists.

3.  Minimal rectal wall thickening which may relate to underdistention but
appears chronic. Clinical correlation is recommended for evaluation of
proctitis.

4.  Questionable cholelithiasis.  Of note, abdominal ultrasound in ___ was
normal.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST ___ AT ___ HOURS.

HISTORY:  Hiccups.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  The lungs are clear without consolidation or edema.  The cardiac
silhouette is markedly enlarged but stable.  Blunting of the left costophrenic
angle is evident anteriorly however no blunting is noted posteriorly.  This
may be due to a small loculated anterior effusion or scarring.  No
pneumothorax is evident.  The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiomegaly.  Small loculated right effusion versus scarring. 
No acute pulmonary process.
